name: Burghley House

dates.altered: The south side was altered by Capability Brown circa 1763-5. The entry records that the right-hand of the two low projecting wings on the north front was demolished in the C18, and that the west front's round-arched bay carries wrought iron gates by Jean Tijou.
dates.note: The register prints 'Circa 1555 to circa 1587'; its own Parks and Gardens entry 1000359 prints 'Building began in 1555'. Both hedge and both are recorded.

refs.note: The Register of Parks and Gardens entry for the setting, 'Date first listed: 16-Jan-1985'. Its historical development section opens 'Burghley House was built by William Cecil, Lord High Treasurer to Elizabeth I, who was created Baron Burghley in 1571. Building began in 1555 and continued for a long period, into the 1580s.' and it describes the house separately as 'one of the largest Elizabethan mansions in the country, erected by William Cecil Lord Burghley between 1555 and 1587'. AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS NOTE PRINTED 'Burghley House was built by William Cecil, Building began in 1555' AS THOUGH IT WERE ONE PRINTED SENTENCE: that is a search-result summary, which joins discontinuous spans, and twenty words are elided at the comma. The tell is the capital letter after a comma. Corrected by re-extracting the page, 5 Sep 2026; the note is prose and no checker reads it.

quotes.text: Circa 1555 to circa 1587. One of the largest of the Elizabethan mansions. An earlier house on the site with remains of St Michaels Priory, incorporated in the present house, came into the possession of Richard Cecil between 1508 and 1528. Richard Cecil's son William Cecil Lord Burghley built the mansion. Built of Barnack stone. The hall with double hammer beam roof and the vaulted kitchen are the earliest parts and form the east side.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details. The entry is in the legacy continuous-prose format, which carries no MATERIALS/PLAN/EXTERIOR headings and no page numbering; this is the span the first extract returned.

quotes.text: Three storeys, at the corners 3 storey and attic square towers with octagonal turrets with ogee cupolas. West front dated 1577 is 1:3:3:3:1 bays with projecting bay windows in the recesses between the angle towers and the central 4 storey entrance tower which has 4 octagonal corner turrets with ogee cupolas and a 3 storeyed canted bay window above a round arch bay with fine wrought iron gates by Jean Tijou. Openwork cresting over the parapet.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, continuation of the same description. No section heading and no page marker: a list entry is not paginated.

quotes.text: The south side altered by Capability Brown circa 1763-5, 3 storeys, the top storey has blind windows, 12 bays the ground floor has 9 bay arcade and a C17 segmental pediment over the central entrance.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, continuation of the same description. No section heading and no page marker: a list entry is not paginated.

quotes.text: The north front dated 1586 has projecting canted feature with ground floor loggia with semi-circular bay at centre and quater-circle bays in the angles, and with crestings and obelisks. Low projecting wing on the left (northeast) with end tower with octagonal top stage with ogee cap, the corresponding right hand wing having been demolished in C18.
quotes.page: Official list entry, Details, continuation of the same description. No section heading and no page marker: a list entry is not paginated.

quotes.text: East side of the courtyard has large central tower in 4 stages, the ground and first stage have large coffered arches. A splayed bay above, each storey flanked by pilastered niches, with superimposed arches. Above is a square clock tower dated 1585 supported by lions and with obelisks at the corners, and surmounted by a huge obelisk spire.
